text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Bundesbank chairman Hans Tietmeyer, who was in Portugal yesterday to attend celebrations marking the 150th anniversary of the Bank of Portugal, said sustained reductions in state deficits were essential components in the consideration of which countries would qualify to join a European single currency.
- Justice Ministry prepares new bankrupcy code. Justice Minister Jose Vera Jardim expects to present the blueprint to the cabinet in December.
- The 2,630 escudos fixed price in the privatisation of a 13.22 percent stake in Banco Totta & Acores (BTA) yesterday was considered to be "a good surprise" by the market, analysts told the paper.
- Bundesbank chairman Hans Tietmeyer said that under a European single currency system, interest rates would only come down if the euro was at least as strong as the German mark.
- Portugal's main trade union the CGTP wants a minimum wage of 60,000 escudos a month and shops to close on Sundays and Bank holidays.
- The government proposed increases in civil servants' salaries in 1997 of 2.6 percent, the newspaper learned.
- The cabinet is to consider the 1996 supplementary budget tomrrow.
